title: Finding out what a pack really does before you install it
hook: A custom node is Python that runs with your rights as soon as ComfyUI starts. Learn to read one first: the order to read files, what runs when, and what to write down.

verified.claim: ComfyUI's security policy says custom nodes are arbitrary Python code, trusted as any other software you install.
main.py runs each pack's prestartup_script.py before the rest of ComfyUI starts.
load_custom_node executes the pack's module on import, then reads WEB_DIRECTORY so the pack's JavaScript is served to the browser.
The lab's file is made up by us, and is read as text and never run.
The graph ran on a CPU.

unchecked: Reading a pack can't prove that it is safe. We say what to look for, and nothing here certifies any pack.
Our line reader in the lab is small and easily fooled, as CU-381 shows. Real reading needs a human.
The list of patterns is about common cases. A careful author of bad code can avoid all of them.
